facts.fact: The Ministry of Health's National Health Sector Policy 2021-2030 states that civil registration and vital statistics in The Gambia is 'currently paper-based' (section 5.3.5); the policy gives no date for the statement, so the document's published date is used.

The Ministry of Health's policy describes CRVS as currently paper-based and says there is 'a need to establish a functional electronic CRVS' for births, deaths, marriages and divorces in all regions; no event is stated as registered digitally. Undated in the text; the document's published date is used.

The National Health Sector Policy 2021-2030 sets out, under its CRVS heading, the need to establish a functional electronic CRVS and names as the primary intervention an integrated real-time data management system for immunisation and birth registration; it lists a costed National Health Sector Strategic Plan 2021-2025 as its implementing document. Undated in the text; the document's published date is used.

The policy lists 'Births & Deaths Registration' among the Ministry of Health's own institutions and units that took part in drafting it (annex 4, item 26), and places CRVS under the ministry's health management information system chapter. Undated in the text; the document's published date is used.
